# Adjudication Task — Chapter 318

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃318화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“떫군.”
  6|
  7|철관음(鐵觀音)을 음미하던 노인이 중얼거렸다.
  8|
  9|나이가 무색하게 딱 벌어진 어깨. 새하얀 수염을 배꼽까지 늘어트린 모습은 신선을 연상케 했다.
 10|
 11|옆에 기대어 놓은 낡은 검 한 자루만 아니었다면 필시 그랬을 터였다.
 12|
 13|“죄, 죄송합니다, 어르신. 제가 아직 아버지만큼의 실력이 되지가 않아…….”
 14|
 15|“아쉽긴 하지만 별수 없지. 주인이 바뀌었으니 차 맛도 바뀌는 것이 당연한 이치. 이만 가 보게.”
 16|
 17|허리를 굽실거리던 다루의 주인이 그 말만을 기다렸다는 듯 사라졌다.
 18|
 19|멀어지는 그의 뒷모습을 바라보던 노인이 찻잔을 어루만졌다.
 20|
 21|“우리 세 사형제는 종종 이곳에 들르고는 했다. 삼십 년도 더 전의 일이지. 그때는 네 사부도 장문인이 아니었고.”
 22|
 23|“그렇군요.”
 24|
 25|탁자 맞은편에 앉아 있던 혁소평이 대답했다.
 26|
 27|한 식경이 넘도록 입을 다물고 노인의 다예(茶艺)를 기다린 그의 목소리는 가뭄의 논바닥처럼 쩍쩍 갈라져 있었다.
 28|
 29|“한 잔 음미해 볼 테냐?”
 30|
 31|부드러운 목소리에는 일말의 강압도 담겨 있지 않았다.
 32|
 33|그러나 눈앞의 노인이 무언가를 권하면 그대로 이행해야 한다. 혁소평뿐만 아니라 다루 곳곳에 포진해 있는 삼십 명의 태을검대(太乙劍隊)도 그 사실을 알고 있었다.
 34|
 35|“감사히 받겠습니다, 사백.”
 36|
 37|공손히 내민 빈 잔, 찻물이 담긴 옥색 다기(茶器)를 집어 든 노인이 손을 기울였다.
 38|
 39|쪼르르륵.
 40|
 41|천천히 잔을 채우기 시작하는 찻물. 동시에 혁소평의 안색이 급변했다.
 42|
 43|“……!”
 44|
 45|“왜 그러느냐?”
 46|
 47|“아……닙니다.”
 48|
 49|말과는 달리 혁소평의 상태는 심상치 않았다. 파르르 떨리는 손과 금방이라도 터질 듯이 붉게 달아오른 얼굴.
 50|
 51|그저 찻물일 뿐인데, 한 방울 한 방울이 찻잔에 닿을 때마다 가공할 압력이 혁소평을 짓눌렀다.
 52|
 53|‘이런 미친……!’
 54|
 55|실로 엄청난 공력이다. 종남파 제일의 기재답게 온갖 영약을 아낌없이 제공받은 혁소평조차 감당할 수 없을 만큼 막강한 기운.
 56|
 57|전신의 공력을 끌어모아 찻잔에 불어넣었지만, 한계는 금방 찾아왔다.
 58|
 59|똑. 쩌저적.
 60|
 61|마지막 한 방울이 떨어진 순간, 혁소평의 손에 들려 있던 잔에 실금이 번지며 찻물이 흘러넘쳤다.
 62|
 63|노인, 태을무정검(太乙無情劍) 황보엄의 눈빛이 깊게 가라앉은 것은 바로 그때였다.
 64|
 65|“네 나이가 올해 몇이더냐.”
 66|
 67|“……이립이 되었습니다.”
 68|
 69|“노부를 마지막으로 본 것은?”
 70|
 71|“십 년 전입니다.”
 72|
 73|“그래, 그랬었지. 종화지회(綜華支會). 바로 그곳에서였어.”
 74|
 75|종화지회. 혹은 화종지회.
 76|
 77|섬서성에 웅크린 두 마리의 용과 호랑이, 화산과 종남은 십 년에 한 번 모임을 가져 자파의 후기지수들을 겨루게 했다.
 78|
 79|공식적인 취지는 비무 대회를 통한 교류와 친목이었지만, 그것이 두 문파의 경쟁이라는 것을 모르는 사람이 없었다.
 80|
 81|“기억나는구나. 네가 백무성, 그놈에게 농락당하는 꼴을 이 두 눈으로 똑똑히 지켜봤었지.”
 82|
 83|“……!”
 84|
 85|혁소평의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.
 86|
 87|어찌 잊을 수 있겠는가. 그날의 패배를. 그리고 본산으로 돌아가자마자 자신을 찾아온 종남제일검의 냉혹한 눈빛을.
 88|
 89|“노부는 네 나이에 태을신공(太乙神功)을 팔 성까지 익혔다. 너는 어떠하냐?”
 90|
 91|“……송구합니다.”
 92|
 93|“십 년이면 강산도 바뀌기 마련이거늘. 네 녀석은 여전히 그 자리에 머물러 있구나.”
 94|
 95|그건 사백님, 당신도 마찬가지이십니다.
 96|
 97|혁소평은 치밀어 오르는 말을 참으려 안간힘을 썼다.
 98|
 99|‘설마 잊으신 것은 아니겠지요. 그날 당신께서 제게 하셨던 그 모든 것들을.’
100|
101|노력 없는 재능은 꽃피울 수 없는 법.
102|
103|무공이 좋았다. 그것이 혁소평이 종남 제일의 기재라 불릴 수 있었던 이유였다. 그는 무공을 좋아했고 피땀 흘려 가며 검을 휘둘렀다.
104|
105|그랬던 그가 서서히 무너진 것은 단순히 모두가 지켜보는 앞에서 화산일학 백무성에게 패배했기 때문이 아니다.
106|
107|“네 녀석이 본문의 이름을 더럽히고 있다는 이야기는 이미 알고 있다. 듣자 하니 서안에서 아주 혁혁한 명성을 떨치고 있다던데.”
108|
109|“사백님…….”
110|
111|“노부가 말하는 중이니라. 그 입 닥치지 못할까.”
112|
113|무미건조했던 황보엄의 목소리는 이제 만년한설보다도 싸늘해져 있었다.
114|
115|“지켜보고 있자니 요지경이 따로 없더군. 위부터 아래까지, 너나 할 것 없이 종남파 현판에 흙탕물을 뿌리고 있어.”
116|
117|위는 노호검객 송일을, 아래는 혁소평을 뜻함이다.
118|
119|하나뿐인 사형이 내상을 입고 쓰러져 있음에도 독설을 퍼붓는 황보엄의 모습에 혁소평과 태을검대 제자들은 다시 한번 깨달았다.
120|
121|‘태을무정검.’
122|
123|그의 별호에 포함된 무정(無情)이라는 두 글자는 적에게만 통용되는 것이 아니라는 것을.
124|
125|“종남파를 이 지경까지 이끌어 온 네 사부도 한심하기는 마찬가지다. 스승님께서는 어찌 그런 놈에게 장문인 직을 물려 주셨는지…….”
126|
127|바로 그때였다. 굳게 다물어져 있던 혁소평의 입술이 열린 것은.
128|
129|“말씀이 과하십니다.”
130|
131|“뭐라?”
132|
133|솨아아아.
134|
135|어디선가 불어온 바람이 혁소평의 전신을 휩쓸었다.
136|
137|아니, 그것은 바람이 아니다. 태을무정검. 종남이 배출해 낸 초절정 고수에게서 흘러나온 막강한 기파(氣波)였다.
138|
139|“늙어서 귀가 어두워진 모양이군. 다시 한번 말해 보아라.”
140|
141|하지만 혁소평은 숨 막히는 압박 속에서도 굴하지 않았다.
142|
143|“말씀이…… 흡. 과하다고 했습니다.”
144|
145|비록 따뜻하고 정감 있는 모습을 보여 주지는 않았으나, 풍운검군은 그의 하나뿐인 사부였다. 또한.
146|
147|“그분은 대종남파의 장문인이십니다. 사백께서도 소질과 같은 종남파의 제자, 장문인에 대한 예의를 갖추십시오.”
148|
149|“장문인에 대한 예의?”
150|
151|순간 황보엄의 눈동자에 기광이 번뜩였다.
152|
153|한때 종남파 장문인의 자리에 가장 가까웠던 것은 그였다.
154|
155|같은 스승을 둔 사형과 사제가 있었으나 경쟁 상대는 아니었다. 두 사람 중 누구도 자신의 무공과 독심(毒心)을 따라올 수 없었으니까.
156|
157|종남파의 장문인은 황보엄, 자신이 되어야 했다. 그것이 순리였다.
158|
159|“한데 네까짓 놈이 무얼 안다고 감히……!”
160|
161|노호성을 내지르려던 황보엄이 문득 입을 닫았다.
162|
163|혁소평의 흔들리지 않는 눈빛. 그리고 태을검대에 속한 종남파 제자들 사이로 흐르는 묘한 기류를 느꼈기 때문이었다.
164|
165|‘이놈들이.’
166|
167|황보엄의 눈빛이 차갑게 가라앉았다. 동시에 그의 전신에서 뿜어져 나오던 강대한 기파가 천천히 수그러들었다.
168|
169|새하얀 수염에 덮여 있던 황보엄의 입술이 달싹였다.
170|
171|“대종남파의 장문인이라…….”
172|
173|황보엄은 채 반도 비워 내지 않은 찻잔을 들어 깨끗이 비웠다. 주름진 미간에 깊은 골이 움푹 파였다.
174|
175|“역시 떫군. 주인이 바뀌니 맛도 향도, 예전 같지 않아.”
176|
177|“……!”
178|
179|“대종남파? 웃기는 소리. 작금의 종남은 사상누각이나 다름없다. 네놈이 실의에 빠져 주색잡기나 하는 동안, 노부는 사문을 일으키기 위해 힘쓰고 있었느니라.”
180|
181|“그게 무슨…….”
182|
183|혁소평의 목소리에 의문이 깃들었다.
184|
185|본산에서도 두문불출하는 황보엄이 아니었던가. 사형인 노호검객이 심각한 내상을 입고 귀환했을 당시에도 얼굴 한 번 비추지 않았던 그다.
186|
187|‘그런데 어떻게…….’
188|
189|혁소평의 생각은 이어지지 못했다. 다음 순간, 다루에 들어온 일단의 무리 때문이었다.
190|
191|그들의 선두에는 등장만으로도 주위를 환하게 만드는 묘령의 여인이 있었다.
192|
193|“용봉표국의 소국주 주화란이 태을무정검 황보 대협을 뵙습니다.”
194|
195|은비화(隱匕花) 주화란. 그녀의 당찬 인사에 황보엄의 입꼬리가 솟구쳤다.
196|
197|“그래. 의뢰한 물건은 잘 가져왔나?”
198|
199|풍성한 수염을 쓰다듬는 그의 눈빛은 알 수 없는 빛으로 번쩍이고 있었다.
200|
201|
202|
203|* * *
204|
205|
206|
207|“그런데 태을무정검이 누구야?”
208|
209|스피드 개건이 퉁명스럽게 대답했다.
210|
211|“태을무정검이 누구긴. 태을무정검이지.”
212|
213|“기방아. 오 성의 항룡십팔장과 칠 성의 화염신장. 어느 것이 더 강한지 궁금해지지 않니?”
214|
215|“……태을무정검 황보엄. 노호검객 송일의 사제이자 현 종남파 장문인 풍운검군의 사형이다.”
216|
217|역시 무림인 백과사전. 이럴 때 써먹으려고 데려온 건 아닌데, 여러모로 쓸모가 있다.
218|
219|‘냄새나는 것만 빼면.’
220|
221|내심 중얼거리며 걸음을 옮겼다.
222|
223|지금 우리는 등왕루라는 이름의 다루를 향해 이동하는 중이었다. 나란히 걷던 궁기방은 썩 마음에 안 든다는 기색으로 중얼거렸다.
224|
225|“내가 줄곧 생각해 봤는데, 이건 좋은 선택이 아닌 것 같다.”
226|
227|“왜?”
228|
229|“생각보다 사안이 커. 다른 사람도 아니고 태을무정검이라니. 차라리 장문인인 풍운검군은 말이라도 통하지, 그 사람은…….”
230|
231|궁기방은 말을 잇지 못하고 고개를 절레절레 흔들었다.
232|
233|“왜, 어느 정도길래. 실제로 만난 적이라도 있어?”
234|
235|“사부님을 곁에서 딱 한 번. 그리고 생각했지. 다시는 만나기 싫은 상대라고.”
236|
237|궁기방의 반응을 보니 첫인상이 어지간히 더러웠던 모양이다.
238|
239|질색하는 표정으로 몸을 부르르 떨던 녀석이 슬쩍 눈짓했다.
240|
241|“굳이 나한테 물어볼 필요도 없다. 이웃집 사정은 이웃이 아는 법이니까.”
242|
243|궁기방의 시선 끝에는 아까부터 말 한마디 없이 묵묵히 걷기만 하는 백무성이 있었다.
244|
245|늘 편안한 미소를 머금고 있던 그의 얼굴은 돌처럼 딱딱하게 굳은 지 오래였다.
246|
247|오케이, 느낌 팍 오네.
248|
249|‘태을무정검이라.’
250|
251|무림을 경험하다 보면 몇 가지 재미있는 부분을 느낄 수가 있는데, 그중 하나가 바로 별호다.
252|
253|별호에는 그 사람의 일부가 녹아 있다. 어느 병기를 주로 사용하는지, 혹은 어느 성격을 지녔는지.
254|
255|태을무정검 황보엄의 경우는 둘 다였다.
256|
257|‘무정. 이 두 글자만 봐도 대충 사이즈가 보이네.’
258|
259|허허 웃는 동네 할아버지는 아니라는 것에 혁무진의 손모가지를 걸 수도 있다. 부족하다면 발모가지도.
260|
261|그때 궁기방이 초조한 목소리로 말했다.
262|
263|“지금이라도 늦지 않았다.”
264|
265|“응? 뭐가?”
266|
267|“문파 간의 일에 개입하는 건 잡음이 생길 가능성이 크다. 상대가 종남파의 태을무정검이라면 더더욱 그렇지.”
268|
269|“그래서?”
270|
271|“그래서긴 뭘 그래서야. 허튼 생각 말고 사천이나 가자는 말이다!”
272|

“You go too far.”

“What did you say?”

*Whoosh.*

A gust swept over Hyuk Sopyung’s entire body.

No—it was not wind.

[P71]
It was a powerful wave of qi flowing from the Taeeul Merciless Sword, a Supreme Peak master produced by Zhongnan.

[P72]
“I must be going deaf in my old age. Say that again.”

[P73]

[P74]
“You… *ngh.* You go too far.”

[P75]
Though the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord had never shown him warmth or affection, he was still Hyuk Sopyung’s one and only Master. And more than that—

[P76]
“He is the Sect Leader of the Great Zhongnan Sect. You are a Disciple of Zhongnan, just as this junior is. Show the Sect Leader the respect he is due.”

[P77]
“Respect for the Sect Leader?”

[P78]
A sharp gleam flashed through Hwangbo Eom’s eyes.

[P79]
There had been a time when no one stood closer to the position of Zhongnan Sect Leader than he did.

[P80]
He had a Senior Brother and Junior Brother under the same Master, but neither had been a true rival. Neither could match his martial prowess or his ruthlessness.

[P81]
Hwangbo Eom should have become the Sect Leader of Zhongnan. It was only natural.

[P82]
“And what could a nobody like you possibly know to dare…!”

[P83]
Hwangbo Eom was about to roar when he abruptly closed his mouth.

[P84]
He had noticed Hyuk Sopyung’s unwavering gaze. He had also sensed the strange current passing among the Zhongnan disciples of the Taeeul Sword Unit.

[P85]
*These bastards.*

[P86]
Hwangbo Eom’s gaze turned cold. At the same time, the powerful aura pouring from his body slowly subsided.

[P87]
His lips moved beneath his snow-white beard.

[P88]
“The Sect Leader of the Great Zhongnan Sect…”

[P89]
Hwangbo Eom lifted his still more than half-full teacup and drained it. Deep furrows appeared between his wrinkled brows.

[P90]
“Still astringent. With a new owner, neither the flavor nor the fragrance is what it used to be.”

[P91]
“…!”

[P92]
“The Great Zhongnan Sect? What a joke. Zhongnan today is nothing more than a castle built on sand. While you wallowed in despair and wasted your days on wine, women, and gambling, this old man was working to restore our sect.”

[P93]
“What do you mean…?”

[P94]
Confusion colored Hyuk Sopyung’s voice.

[P95]
Hadn’t Hwangbo Eom shut himself away even at the main sect? He had not shown his face once, not even when his Senior Brother, the Roaring Fury Swordsman, returned with severe internal injuries.

[P96]
*Then how…?*

[P97]
Hyuk Sopyung’s thoughts were cut short when a group entered the teahouse.

[P98]
At their head was a young woman whose mere presence seemed to brighten her surroundings.

[P99]
“I am Ju Hwaran, Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau. I pay my respects to Great Hero Hwangbo, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.”

[P100]
Ju Hwaran, the Dagger Hidden Flower.

[P101]
At her bold greeting, the corners of Hwangbo Eom’s mouth curled upward.

[P102]
“Good. Did you bring the item I requested?”

[P103]
He stroked his thick beard, his eyes flashing with an unreadable light.

[P104]
* * *

[P105]
“By the way, who’s the Taeeul Merciless Sword?”

[P106]
Speed Beggar answered gruffly.

[P107]
“Who else would the Taeeul Merciless Sword be? He’s the Taeeul Merciless Sword.”

[P108]
“Gibang. Aren’t you curious which is stronger—the Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms at five-tenths power or the Flame Divine Palm at seven-tenths?”

[P109]
“…”

[P110]
“The Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom. He’s the Junior Brother of the Roaring Fury Swordsman, Song Il, and the Senior Brother of the current Zhongnan Sect Leader, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord.”

[P111]
As expected of a walking encyclopedia of the Murim. I hadn’t brought him along for moments like this, but he was useful in all sorts of ways.

[P112]
*Except for the smell.*

[P113]
I muttered inwardly as I kept walking.

[P114]
We were on our way to a teahouse called Tengwang Pavilion. Gung Gibang walked beside me, looking deeply displeased.

[P115]
“I’ve been thinking about this, and I don’t think it’s a good idea.”

[P116]
“Why?”

[P117]
“This is bigger than I expected. And it isn’t just anyone—it’s the Taeeul Merciless Sword. At least you can reason with the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, but that man…”

[P118]
Gung Gibang trailed off and shook his head.

[P119]
“Why? How bad is he? Have you met him before?”

[P120]
“Once, while I was with my Master. That was enough to make me never want to see him again.”

[P121]
Judging by Gung Gibang’s reaction, Hwangbo Eom must have made one hell of a first impression.

[P122]
He shuddered in disgust, then glanced sideways.

[P123]
“You don’t need to ask me. No one knows a household better than its neighbor.”

[P124]
His gaze fell on Baek Museong, who had been walking in silence for some time.

[P125]
The face that usually wore a relaxed smile had long since hardened like stone.

[P126]
*Okay. I get the picture.*

[P127]
*The Taeeul Merciless Sword.*

[P128]
As you spent time in the Murim, you started noticing a few interesting things. One of them was martial epithets.

[P129]
An epithet contained a piece of the person it belonged to. Sometimes it told you what weapon they favored. Other times, it revealed their personality.

[P130]
In Hwangbo Eom’s case, it did both.

[P131]
*Merciless. That word alone tells me more or less what I need to know.*

[P132]
I’d bet Hyuk Mujin’s wrist that he wasn’t some genial neighborhood grandpa who chuckled all day. If that wasn’t enough, I’d throw in his ankle too.

[P133]
Gung Gibang spoke anxiously.

[P134]
“It’s not too late to turn back.”

[P135]
“Hm? Turn back from what?”

[P136]
“Interfering in matters between sects is bound to cause trouble. Even more so when the other party is the Zhongnan Sect’s Taeeul Merciless Sword.”

[P137]
“So?”

[P138]
“What do you mean, ‘so’? I’m telling you to forget this nonsense and go to Sichuan!”

[P139]
I blinked innocently.

[P140]
“What the hell are you talking about?”

[P141]
“Huh?”

[P142]
“Who’s interfering? We’re just going to drink some tea. Isn’t that right, Young Hero Cheong?”

[P143]
Cheongpung, who was chewing the candied sweets I had bought to keep him quiet, answered enthusiastically.

[P144]
“Yes! We’re going to drink tea!”

[P145]
Gung Gibang stared at him incredulously.

[P146]
“Didn’t you say earlier that you’d already had tea?”

[P147]
“Uh… Well…”

[P148]
No wonder his answer had sounded so evasive.

[P149]
Cheongpung had already polished off the sweets in the blink of an eye. He sucked on his fingers and looked back and forth between Gung Gibang and me.

[P150]
His eyes brimmed with longing as they swept over the street stalls laden with snacks.

[P151]
“Young Hero Cheong, you’ve never had tea before. Right?”

[P152]
As I spoke, I spread one hand wide and waved it over Gung Gibang’s shoulder. Five more candied sweets were added to Cheongpung’s share, and he nodded eagerly.

[P153]
“That’s right! I’ve never had tea before! My butt’s itching to get to the teahouse!”

[P154]
“You heard him.”

[P155]
His will to fight shattered, Gung Gibang tore at his matted hair.

[P156]
“Damn it. If Master beats me with the Dog-Beating Staff later, I’m telling him this was all your fault.”

[P157]
“Go ahead. My Master is the Fire King.”

[P158]
“You miserable bastard. You’re worse than a dog.”

[P159]
“Stop whining and keep walking. What about you, Mujin? Got a problem?”

[P160]
Hyuk Mujin looked at me hopefully.

[P161]
“Am I allowed to say so?”

[P162]
“Sure. If you want to die.”

[P163]
“…”

[P164]
“All right. We’re almost there.”

[P165]
The weathered signboard bearing the name Tengwang Pavilion drew steadily closer.

[P166]
I strode onward until I finally stopped before the teahouse door.

[P167]
*Well, this is no joke.*

[P168]
The Taeeul Merciless Sword. The greatest swordsman Zhongnan could boast of. I could feel the aura of a Supreme Peak master beyond the door, along with the presence of dozens of people carrying considerable qi.

[P169]
The pack frame on my shoulders suddenly felt heavier.

[P170]
“Old Master, don’t worry. No matter what happens, I’ll protect you.”

[P171]
“Nothing will happen,” I muttered softly, then threw open the door.

### Tone and Style

His words notwithstanding, Hyuk Sopyung was clearly struggling. His hand trembled, and his face flushed so red it seemed ready to burst.

[P26]
It was only tea, yet every drop that struck the cup bore down on him with terrifying pressure.

[P27]
*What the hell…?*

[P28]
The sheer amount of internal energy was staggering. Even Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan Sect’s greatest prodigy, could not withstand its overwhelming force despite having been supplied with every elixir the sect could spare.

[P29]
He drew up all the internal energy in his body and poured it into the teacup, but he reached his limit almost immediately.

[P30]
*Tap. Crack.*

[P31]
The instant the last drop fell, a hairline crack spread through the cup in Hyuk Sopyung’s hand, and tea spilled over the rim.

[P32]
That was when the old man’s gaze darkened.

[P33]
He was Hwangbo Eom, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.

[P34]
“How old are you this year?”

[P35]
“…I have reached thirty.”

[P36]
“When did you last see this old man?”

[P37]
“Ten years ago.”

[P38]
“Yes, that’s right. The Huashan–Zhongnan gathering. That was where we last met.”

[P39]
The Huashan–Zhongnan gathering. Or the Zhongnan–Huashan gathering.

[P40]
Huashan and Zhongnan—the dragon and tiger crouched in Shaanxi Province—held a gathering once every ten years where their young prodigies competed against one another.

[P41]
Its official purpose was to foster friendship and exchange through duels, but everyone knew it was really a competition between the two sects.

[P42]
“I remember now. I watched with my own eyes as that bastard Baek Museong toyed with you.”

[P43]
“…!”

[P44]
Hyuk Sopyung’s eyelids trembled.

[P45]
How could he forget? The defeat he had suffered that day. The merciless gaze of The First Sword of Zhongnan, who had sought him out the moment he returned to the main sect.

[P46]
“At your age, this old man had already mastered eight-tenths of the Taeeul Divine Technique. What about you?”

[P47]
“…I apologize.”

[P48]
“Ten years is enough time for mountains and rivers to change. Yet you remain exactly where you were.”

[P49]
*The same goes for you, Senior Martial Uncle.*

[P50]
Hyuk Sopyung fought desperately to hold back the words rising in his throat.

[P51]
*Surely you haven’t forgotten everything you did to me that day.*

[P52]
Talent without effort could never bloom.

[P53]
Hyuk Sopyung loved martial arts. That was why he had been called the Zhongnan Sect’s greatest prodigy. He had devoted himself to martial arts and swung his sword through blood and sweat.

[P54]
But he had not slowly fallen apart simply because Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong, defeated him in front of everyone.

[P55]
“I already know you’ve been disgracing our sect’s name. I hear you’ve made quite a name for yourself in Xi’an.”

[P56]
“Senior Martial Uncle…”

[P57]
“This old man is speaking. Shut your mouth.”

[P58]
Hwangbo Eom’s formerly dispassionate voice had turned colder than eternal ice.

[P59]
“Watching all of you has been quite the farce. From top to bottom, every last one of you is splattering mud across the Zhongnan Sect’s signboard.”

[P60]
By the top, he meant the Roaring Fury Swordsman, Song Il. By the bottom, he meant Hyuk Sopyung.

[P61]
Even with his only Senior Brother laid up by severe internal injuries, Hwangbo Eom continued to spew venom at him. Hyuk Sopyung and the disciples of the Taeeul Sword Unit were reminded once again that the two words in his epithet—

[P62]
*Taeeul Merciless Sword.*

[P63]
—did not apply only to his enemies.

[P64]
“Your Master, who led the Zhongnan Sect into this sorry state, is just as pathetic. Why our Master ever handed the position of Sect Leader to someone like him…”

[P65]
That was when Hyuk Sopyung’s tightly pressed lips finally parted.

[P66]
“You go too far.”

[P67]
“What did you say?”

[P68]
*Whoosh.*

[P69]
A gust swept over Hyuk Sopyung’s entire body.

[P70]
No—it was not wind.

[P71]
It was a powerful wave of qi flowing from the Taeeul Merciless Sword, a Supreme Peak master produced by Zhongnan.

[P72]
“I must be going deaf in my old age. Say that again.”

[P73]
But Hyuk Sopyung did not yield, even beneath the suffocating pressure.

[P74]
“You… *ngh.* You go too far.”

[P75]
Though the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord had never shown him warmth or affection, he was still Hyuk Sopyung’s one and only Master. And more than that—

[P76]
“He is the Sect Leader of the Great Zhongnan Sect. You are a Disciple of Zhongnan, just as this junior is. Show the Sect Leader the respect he is due.”

[P77]
“Respect for the Sect Leader?”

[P78]
A sharp gleam flashed through Hwangbo Eom’s eyes.

[P79]
There had been a time when no one stood closer to the position of Zhongnan Sect Leader than he did.

[P80]
He had a Senior Brother and Junior Brother under the same Master, but neither had been a true rival. Neither could match his martial prowess or his ruthlessness.

[P81]
Hwangbo Eom should have become the Sect Leader of Zhongnan. It was only natural.

[P82]
“And what could a nobody like you possibly know to dare…!”

[P83]
Hwangbo Eom was about to roar when he abruptly closed his mouth.

[P84]
He had noticed Hyuk Sopyung’s unwavering gaze. He had also sensed the strange current passing among the Zhongnan disciples of the Taeeul Sword Unit.

[P85]
*These bastards.*

[P86]
Hwangbo Eom’s gaze turned cold. At the same time, the powerful aura pouring from his body slowly subsided.

[P87]
His lips moved beneath his snow-white beard.

[P88]
“The Sect Leader of the Great Zhongnan Sect…”

[P89]
Hwangbo Eom lifted his still more than half-full teacup and drained it. Deep furrows appeared between his wrinkled brows.

[P90]
“Still astringent. With a new owner, neither the flavor nor the fragrance is what it used to be.”

[P91]
“…!”

[P92]
“The Great Zhongnan Sect? What a joke. Zhongnan today is nothing more than a castle built on sand. While you wallowed in despair and wasted your days on wine, women, and gambling, this old man was working to restore our sect.”

[P93]
“What do you mean…?”

[P94]
Confusion colored Hyuk Sopyung’s voice.

[P95]
Hadn’t Hwangbo Eom shut himself away even at the main sect? He had not shown his face once, not even when his Senior Brother, the Roaring Fury Swordsman, returned with severe internal injuries.

[P96]
*Then how…?*

[P97]
Hyuk Sopyung’s thoughts were cut short when a group entered the teahouse.

[P98]
At their head was a young woman whose mere presence seemed to brighten her surroundings.

[P99]
“I am Ju Hwaran, Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau. I pay my respects to Great Hero Hwangbo, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.”

[P100]
Ju Hwaran, the Dagger Hidden Flower.

[P101]
At her bold greeting, the corners of Hwangbo Eom’s mouth curled upward.

[P102]
“Good. Did you bring the item I requested?”

[P103]
He stroked his thick beard, his eyes flashing with an unreadable light.

[P104]
* * *

[P105]
“By the way, who’s the Taeeul Merciless Sword?”

[P106]
Speed Beggar answered gruffly.

[P107]
“Who else would the Taeeul Merciless Sword be? He’s the Taeeul Merciless Sword.”

[P108]
“Gibang. Aren’t you curious which is stronger—the Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms at five-tenths power or the Flame Divine Palm at seven-tenths?”

[P109]
“…”

[P110]
“The Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom. He’s the Junior Brother of the Roaring Fury Swordsman, Song Il, and the Senior Brother of the current Zhongnan Sect Leader, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord.”

[P111]
As expected of a walking encyclopedia of the Murim. I hadn’t brought him along for moments like this, but he was useful in all sorts of ways.

[P112]
*Except for the smell.*

[P113]
I muttered inwardly as I kept walking.

[P114]
We were on our way to a teahouse called Tengwang Pavilion. Gung Gibang walked beside me, looking deeply displeased.

[P115]
“I’ve been thinking about this, and I don’t think it’s a good idea.”

[P116]
“Why?”

[P117]
“This is bigger than I expected. And it isn’t just anyone—it’s the Taeeul Merciless Sword. At least you can reason with the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, but that man…”

[P118]
Gung Gibang trailed off and shook his head.

[P119]
“Why? How bad is he? Have you met him before?”

[P120]
“Once, while I was with my Master. That was enough to make me never want to see him again.”

[P121]
Judging by Gung Gibang’s reaction, Hwangbo Eom must have made one hell of a first impression.

[P122]
He shuddered in disgust, then glanced sideways.

[P123]
“You don’t need to ask me. No one knows a household better than its neighbor.”

[P124]
His gaze fell on Baek Museong, who had been walking in silence for some time.

[P125]
The face that usually wore a relaxed smile had long since hardened like stone.

[P126]
*Okay. I get the picture.*

[P127]
*The Taeeul Merciless Sword.*

[P128]
As you spent time in the Murim, you started noticing a few interesting things. One of them was martial epithets.

[P129]
An epithet contained a piece of the person it belonged to. Sometimes it told you what weapon they favored. Other times, it revealed their personality.

[P130]
In Hwangbo Eom’s case, it did both.

[P131]
*Merciless. That word alone tells me more or less what I need to know.*

[P132]
I’d bet Hyuk Mujin’s wrist that he wasn’t some genial neighborhood grandpa who chuckled all day. If that wasn’t enough, I’d throw in his ankle too.

[P133]
Gung Gibang spoke anxiously.

[P134]
“It’s not too late to turn back.”

[P135]
“Hm? Turn back from what?”

[P136]
“Interfering in matters between sects is bound to cause trouble. Even more so when the other party is the Zhongnan Sect’s Taeeul Merciless Sword.”

[P137]
“So?”

[P138]
“What do you mean, ‘so’? I’m telling you to forget this nonsense and go to Sichuan!”

[P139]
I blinked innocently.

[P140]
“What the hell are you talking about?”

[P141]
“Huh?”

[P142]
“Who’s interfering? We’re just going to drink some tea. Isn’t that right, Young Hero Cheong?”

[P143]
Cheongpung, who was chewing the candied sweets I had bought to keep him quiet, answered enthusiastically.

[P144]
“Yes! We’re going to drink tea!”

[P145]
Gung Gibang stared at him incredulously.

[P146]
“Didn’t you say earlier that you’d already had tea?”

[P147]
“Uh… Well…”

[P148]
No wonder his answer had sounded so evasive.

[P149]
Cheongpung had already polished off the sweets in the blink of an eye. He sucked on his fingers and looked back and forth between Gung Gibang and me.

[P150]
His eyes brimmed with longing as they swept over the street stalls laden with snacks.

[P151]
“Young Hero Cheong, you’ve never had tea before. Right?”

[P152]
As I spoke, I spread one hand wide and waved it over Gung Gibang’s shoulder. Five more candied sweets were added to Cheongpung’s share, and he nodded eagerly.

[P153]
“That’s right! I’ve never had tea before! My butt’s itching to get to the teahouse!”

[P154]
“You heard him.”

[P155]
His will to fight shattered, Gung Gibang tore at his matted hair.

[P156]
“Damn it. If Master beats me with the Dog-Beating Staff later, I’m telling him this was all your fault.”

[P157]
“Go ahead. My Master is the Fire King.”

[P158]
“You miserable bastard. You’re worse than a dog.”

[P159]
“Stop whining and keep walking. What about you, Mujin? Got a problem?”

[P160]
Hyuk Mujin looked at me hopefully.

[P161]
“Am I allowed to say so?”

[P162]
“Sure. If you want to die.”

[P163]
“…”

[P164]
“All right. We’re almost there.”

[P165]
The weathered signboard bearing the name Tengwang Pavilion drew steadily closer.

[P166]
I strode onward until I finally stopped before the teahouse door.

[P167]
*Well, this is no joke.*

[P168]
The Taeeul Merciless Sword. The greatest swordsman Zhongnan could boast of. I could feel the aura of a Supreme Peak master beyond the door, along with the presence of dozens of people carrying considerable qi.

[P169]
The pack frame on my shoulders suddenly felt heavier.

[P170]
“Old Master, don’t worry. No matter what happens, I’ll protect you.”

[P171]
“Nothing will happen,” I muttered softly, then threw open the door.

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 318

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃318화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“떫군.”
  6|
  7|철관음(鐵觀音)을 음미하던 노인이 중얼거렸다.
  8|
  9|나이가 무색하게 딱 벌어진 어깨. 새하얀 수염을 배꼽까지 늘어트린 모습은 신선을 연상케 했다.
 10|
 11|옆에 기대어 놓은 낡은 검 한 자루만 아니었다면 필시 그랬을 터였다.
 12|
 13|“죄, 죄송합니다, 어르신. 제가 아직 아버지만큼의 실력이 되지가 않아…….”
 14|
 15|“아쉽긴 하지만 별수 없지. 주인이 바뀌었으니 차 맛도 바뀌는 것이 당연한 이치. 이만 가 보게.”
 16|
 17|허리를 굽실거리던 다루의 주인이 그 말만을 기다렸다는 듯 사라졌다.
 18|
 19|멀어지는 그의 뒷모습을 바라보던 노인이 찻잔을 어루만졌다.
 20|
 21|“우리 세 사형제는 종종 이곳에 들르고는 했다. 삼십 년도 더 전의 일이지. 그때는 네 사부도 장문인이 아니었고.”
 22|
 23|“그렇군요.”
 24|
 25|탁자 맞은편에 앉아 있던 혁소평이 대답했다.
 26|
 27|한 식경이 넘도록 입을 다물고 노인의 다예(茶艺)를 기다린 그의 목소리는 가뭄의 논바닥처럼 쩍쩍 갈라져 있었다.
 28|
 29|“한 잔 음미해 볼 테냐?”
 30|
 31|부드러운 목소리에는 일말의 강압도 담겨 있지 않았다.
 32|
 33|그러나 눈앞의 노인이 무언가를 권하면 그대로 이행해야 한다. 혁소평뿐만 아니라 다루 곳곳에 포진해 있는 삼십 명의 태을검대(太乙劍隊)도 그 사실을 알고 있었다.
 34|
 35|“감사히 받겠습니다, 사백.”
 36|
 37|공손히 내민 빈 잔, 찻물이 담긴 옥색 다기(茶器)를 집어 든 노인이 손을 기울였다.
 38|
 39|쪼르르륵.
 40|
 41|천천히 잔을 채우기 시작하는 찻물. 동시에 혁소평의 안색이 급변했다.
 42|
 43|“……!”
 44|
 45|“왜 그러느냐?”
 46|
 47|“아……닙니다.”
 48|
 49|말과는 달리 혁소평의 상태는 심상치 않았다. 파르르 떨리는 손과 금방이라도 터질 듯이 붉게 달아오른 얼굴.
 50|
 51|그저 찻물일 뿐인데, 한 방울 한 방울이 찻잔에 닿을 때마다 가공할 압력이 혁소평을 짓눌렀다.
 52|
 53|‘이런 미친……!’
 54|
 55|실로 엄청난 공력이다. 종남파 제일의 기재답게 온갖 영약을 아낌없이 제공받은 혁소평조차 감당할 수 없을 만큼 막강한 기운.
 56|
 57|전신의 공력을 끌어모아 찻잔에 불어넣었지만, 한계는 금방 찾아왔다.
 58|
 59|똑. 쩌저적.
 60|
 61|마지막 한 방울이 떨어진 순간, 혁소평의 손에 들려 있던 잔에 실금이 번지며 찻물이 흘러넘쳤다.
 62|
 63|노인, 태을무정검(太乙無情劍) 황보엄의 눈빛이 깊게 가라앉은 것은 바로 그때였다.
 64|
 65|“네 나이가 올해 몇이더냐.”
 66|
 67|“……이립이 되었습니다.”
 68|
 69|“노부를 마지막으로 본 것은?”
 70|
 71|“십 년 전입니다.”
 72|
 73|“그래, 그랬었지. 종화지회(綜華支會). 바로 그곳에서였어.”
 74|
 75|종화지회. 혹은 화종지회.
 76|
 77|섬서성에 웅크린 두 마리의 용과 호랑이, 화산과 종남은 십 년에 한 번 모임을 가져 자파의 후기지수들을 겨루게 했다.
 78|
 79|공식적인 취지는 비무 대회를 통한 교류와 친목이었지만, 그것이 두 문파의 경쟁이라는 것을 모르는 사람이 없었다.
 80|
 81|“기억나는구나. 네가 백무성, 그놈에게 농락당하는 꼴을 이 두 눈으로 똑똑히 지켜봤었지.”
 82|
 83|“……!”
 84|
 85|혁소평의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.
 86|
 87|어찌 잊을 수 있겠는가. 그날의 패배를. 그리고 본산으로 돌아가자마자 자신을 찾아온 종남제일검의 냉혹한 눈빛을.
 88|
 89|“노부는 네 나이에 태을신공(太乙神功)을 팔 성까지 익혔다. 너는 어떠하냐?”
 90|
 91|“……송구합니다.”
 92|
 93|“십 년이면 강산도 바뀌기 마련이거늘. 네 녀석은 여전히 그 자리에 머물러 있구나.”
 94|
 95|그건 사백님, 당신도 마찬가지이십니다.
 96|
 97|혁소평은 치밀어 오르는 말을 참으려 안간힘을 썼다.
 98|
 99|‘설마 잊으신 것은 아니겠지요. 그날 당신께서 제게 하셨던 그 모든 것들을.’
100|
101|노력 없는 재능은 꽃피울 수 없는 법.
102|
103|무공이 좋았다. 그것이 혁소평이 종남 제일의 기재라 불릴 수 있었던 이유였다. 그는 무공을 좋아했고 피땀 흘려 가며 검을 휘둘렀다.
104|
105|그랬던 그가 서서히 무너진 것은 단순히 모두가 지켜보는 앞에서 화산일학 백무성에게 패배했기 때문이 아니다.
106|
107|“네 녀석이 본문의 이름을 더럽히고 있다는 이야기는 이미 알고 있다. 듣자 하니 서안에서 아주 혁혁한 명성을 떨치고 있다던데.”
108|
109|“사백님…….”
110|
111|“노부가 말하는 중이니라. 그 입 닥치지 못할까.”
112|
113|무미건조했던 황보엄의 목소리는 이제 만년한설보다도 싸늘해져 있었다.
114|
115|“지켜보고 있자니 요지경이 따로 없더군. 위부터 아래까지, 너나 할 것 없이 종남파 현판에 흙탕물을 뿌리고 있어.”
116|
117|위는 노호검객 송일을, 아래는 혁소평을 뜻함이다.
118|
119|하나뿐인 사형이 내상을 입고 쓰러져 있음에도 독설을 퍼붓는 황보엄의 모습에 혁소평과 태을검대 제자들은 다시 한번 깨달았다.
120|
121|‘태을무정검.’
122|
123|그의 별호에 포함된 무정(無情)이라는 두 글자는 적에게만 통용되는 것이 아니라는 것을.
124|
125|“종남파를 이 지경까지 이끌어 온 네 사부도 한심하기는 마찬가지다. 스승님께서는 어찌 그런 놈에게 장문인 직을 물려 주셨는지…….”
126|
127|바로 그때였다. 굳게 다물어져 있던 혁소평의 입술이 열린 것은.
128|
129|“말씀이 과하십니다.”
130|
131|“뭐라?”
132|
133|솨아아아.
134|
135|어디선가 불어온 바람이 혁소평의 전신을 휩쓸었다.
136|
137|아니, 그것은 바람이 아니다. 태을무정검. 종남이 배출해 낸 초절정 고수에게서 흘러나온 막강한 기파(氣波)였다.
138|
139|“늙어서 귀가 어두워진 모양이군. 다시 한번 말해 보아라.”
140|
141|하지만 혁소평은 숨 막히는 압박 속에서도 굴하지 않았다.
142|
143|“말씀이…… 흡. 과하다고 했습니다.”
144|
145|비록 따뜻하고 정감 있는 모습을 보여 주지는 않았으나, 풍운검군은 그의 하나뿐인 사부였다. 또한.
146|
147|“그분은 대종남파의 장문인이십니다. 사백께서도 소질과 같은 종남파의 제자, 장문인에 대한 예의를 갖추십시오.”
148|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
